items.title: Fred Lipsius interviewed by Monk Rowe. Boston, Massachusetts, July 25, 2018
items.q: Plays really great, not modern, but we’re very friendly.

ctx.x: There was a big, fairly significant turnover after the first Blood, Sweat & Tears record. Did that come internally or was that partly from like Columbia Records.

I don’t think they had anything to do with that. Look, I’m one-ninth. And I tell people, I’ve written stories about Blood, Sweat & Tears, little things, without putting anybody down because I just don’t want to do that. Because there’s different views. I’m not perfect you know. So there’s people that don’t like me as a teacher. They don’t like me because I’m a nice guy, they don’t like my smile. It’s just the way it is. You know, that’s the way it is. Other people think I’m the best piano player in the world, or,…

or something but I was playing my alto and he was in another room down the hallway at Berklee. Everybody else was gone, it was nighttime. And he was nice enough to fix my horn or do something. So I was really up on playing my horn. I wasn’t playing all the time, but it just felt great. So I go into his room and I played a couple of notes, which he has rarely heard me play.
